stem: A febrile transplant recipient with a central venous line is started on empiric antibiotics after cultures are obtained. Which initial antibiotic choice aligns with standard bacterial-infection references?

options.text: Begin vancomycin until the organism is identified when a central venous line is present
Withhold all antibiotics until culture results return in two weeks
Oral metronidazole alone is always sufficient for central-line bacteremia
Empiric therapy never covers line-related infection when a CVL is present

explanation.rationale_correct: Bacterial infection treatment includes broad-spectrum antibiotics after cultures are obtained; if a central venous line is present, vancomycin is begun until the organism is identified.

rationale_incorrect.B: Broad-spectrum antibiotics are administered after cultures are obtained rather than withholding all therapy.
rationale_incorrect.C: Line-related bacteremia management includes vancomycin when a CVL is present rather than metronidazole alone in every case.
rationale_incorrect.D: CVL presence specifically guides empiric vancomycin therapy.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 13, Post-Transplant Complications → bacterial infection → Treatment → h.i.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: If a CVL is present, begin vancomycin until the organism is identified

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 13 → bacterial infection → h.i. (vancomycin when CVL present until organism identified); PDF p. 734 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. CVL/vancomycin empiric therapy angle distinct from bacterial-sign combo (cctc-3132) and pediatric irritability item (cctc-3131); anchor verified on Cupples p. 734.

stem: When managing a febrile transplant recipient colonized with vancomycin-resistant enterococcus (VRE), which antibiotic consideration aligns with standard references?

options.text: Linezolid should be considered if the patient is colonized with VRE
VRE colonization requires no change in empiric antibiotic selection
VRE colonization mandates routine oral metronidazole monotherapy for all fevers
Colonized patients should never receive any empiric antibiotics

explanation.rationale_correct: When a central venous line is present, vancomycin is started until the organism is identified; if the patient is colonized with VRE, linezolid should be considered.

rationale_incorrect.B: VRE colonization influences antibiotic selection rather than being ignored.
rationale_incorrect.C: Linezolid is specifically considered for VRE colonization rather than universal metronidazole monotherapy.
rationale_incorrect.D: Empiric broad-spectrum therapy after cultures is still indicated with adjustments for colonization status.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 13, Post-Transplant Complications → bacterial infection → Treatment → h.i.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: If the patient is colonized with VRE, linezolid should be considered

stem: A kidney transplant recipient reports cloudy urine and increased drainage odor without fever yet. Which finding aligns with standard bacterial-infection teaching?

options.text: Changes in drainage or output such as purulence, cloudy urine, or altered stool odor may indicate bacterial infection
Cloudy urine never indicates infection in transplant recipients
Drainage changes are expected and never require evaluation
Only fever above 104°F indicates possible bacterial infection

explanation.rationale_correct: Signs of bacterial infection include changes in drainage or output such as purulence, cloudy urine, and changes in stool consistency, amount, or odor.

rationale_incorrect.B: Cloudy urine is specifically listed among output changes that may indicate infection.
rationale_incorrect.C: Drainage and output changes warrant clinical evaluation rather than being dismissed as always expected.
rationale_incorrect.D: Fever is usually ≥101°F (38.5°C), and output changes may occur with or before high fever.

stem: A coordinator is updating bacterial-infection management protocols. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Broad-spectrum antibiotics should be administered after cultures are obtained based on the apparent or suspected etiology of fever.
If a central venous line is present, vancomycin may be started until the organism is identified.
Immunosuppression may be decreased with caution during severe bacterial infection while monitoring for rejection.
Tacrolimus levels never need monitoring during bacterial infection treatment.

explanation.rationale_correct: Culture-directed empiric antibiotics, CVL vancomycin, and cautious immunosuppression reduction with rejection monitoring are supported. Statement IV is false because tacrolimus levels should be closely monitored and reported when not therapeutic.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement III is also true—immunosuppression may be decreased cautiously with rejection monitoring.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement IV is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement IV is false because tacrolimus levels require close monitoring during infection treatment.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Broad-spectrum antibiotics administered after cultures … vancomycin … Immunosuppression may be decreased … Closely monitor tacrolimus levels
